title: Are these 4 Topeka locations truly haunted?
excerpt: Topeka is home to several chilling legends. Explore 4 local sites rumored to be haunted by restless spirits.
content:
Oct. 23, 2026, 4:02 a.m. CT

  • Topeka, Kansas, is home to several locations with reported paranormal activity and ghost stories.
  • A ghostly "Albino Woman" is said to haunt Rochester Cemetery, with legends about her growing more sinister over time.
  • The Kansas Statehouse is reportedly haunted by the spirits of a former employee and a construction worker.
  • Other local legends include friendly spirits at the Historic Topeka Cemetery and demonic activity at a now-demolished church.

Spooky scary skeletons may send shivers down your spine, but Topeka has its own haunts to get your knees shaking.

The capital city is no stranger to ghost stories and terrifying tales.

Here are four that you can find and explore in the Topeka area.

Rochester Cemetery gets an 'Albino Woman' visitor every night

Topeka's Rochester Cemetery, located at 1200 N.W. Rochester Road, has been the center of a spirited rumor.

An "Albino Woman" is said to have haunted the cemetery for generations. The ghostly figure who wanders the grounds is claimed to have long, white hair flowing; stark, white skin; and eyes that glow red or pink.

The rumors claim, the Albino Woman once lived in the area.

Described in Topekan Lisa Hefner Heitz's book "Haunted Kansas," she is a harmless spirit who rose from her grave and walked the cemetery grounds with her poodle.

However, as the years passed and the legend grew, Hefner Heitz said, the character grew increasingly dangerous, with some stories about attacks and even homicides beginning to spread.

Fandom, a website that focuses on urban legends, reported claims of the "Blue Albino Woman" devouring human flesh.

Former employee is said to haunt the Kansas Statehouse

The Kansas Statehouse, located at 300 SW 10th Ave., is the subject of multiple urban legends.

In July 1965, the Topeka Daily Capital reported that 43-year-old Eileen McClain set her lit cigarette on a marble slab 150 feet above the rotunda, then mounted a nearby ledge and leapt to her death. Since then, rumors have stirred of her haunting where she landed and in its basement area.

Stories of the sound of unexplainable footsteps and crying can be heard, according to the Haunted Houses website.

Legends also say a construction worker who died while working at the Statehouse has been haunting the place ever since his death. Stories say that he was never paid his last check, and had no surviving family members. So even in death, he still works and has been heard hammering at night, according to the Kansas Haunted Houses website.

Topeka's historic cemetery could host friendly spirits

Another consecrated area with a ghoulish history is the Historic Topeka Cemetery, located at 1601 SE 10th Ave.

The cemetery, which has existed for over a century and a half, could be prime for encountering some of Topeka's oldest residents' afterlives.

Some cemetery staff tell stories of an elderly man chatting up grave diggers then vanishing. Others claim to see a little ghost girl.

Former Harrison Street Church carries tales of hauntings

A 94-year-old former church, located at 1600 S.W. Harrison, was featured in a 2009 episode of the former A&E reality television series, “Paranormal State.”

While the Harrison Street Church was later demolished by a 2013 fire, the legend can be relived through the episode titled "Church of the D*mned," which can be found on Apple TV.

The season three episode followed a Topeka family who could no longer do repairs on the church due to the "menacing activity." The segment also includes a scene of reality star Ryan Buell being attacked by a demon.

Stacey Saldanha-Olson is an enterprise reporter for The Topeka Capital-Journal. She can be reached by email at solson@usatodayco.com. Follow her on X @ssaldanhao.
